notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; all 13 wires, 6 resistors, 6 LEDs, the Uno and the breadboard are still needed.

Each channel: Uno pin (7,6,5,4,3,2) -> blue wire -> breadboard column -> 220 ohm resistor across the centre gap -> LED anode; LED cathode column -> short black wire -> ground rail; Uno GND -> same ground rail.
Pin mapping from the image: pin 7 -> LED1 (columns 7/8), pin 6 -> LED2 (10/11), pin 5 -> LED3 (13/14), pin 4 -> LED4 (16/17), pin 3 -> LED5 (19/20), pin 2 -> LED6 (22/23).

The image draws the LEDs in the upper half of the breadboard; the catalogue calls the upper half bank 't' (rows a-e) and the lower half bank 'b' (rows f-j), so I used 't' for the LED/resistor-top side and 'b' for the wire side. Row letters within a strip are arbitrary.
The LED anode is the bent (left) leg in the image and sits in the same column as its resistor; the cathode is the next column to the right and has the black wire to the top ground (tn) rail.
The ground rail is one strip, so tn.1 to tn.7 are the same node; I used different holes only so that each wire has its own hole.
The Uno GND is wired from the GND socket beside pin 13 on the digital header; I used port GND.1 for it.
Resistor legs are interchangeable, so the 1/2 assignment is arbitrary.
